name: Decision matrix
description: Agree what matters, score every option on the same scale, and check whether the ranking survives uncertain assumptions.

walkthroughIntro.inOneLine: Agree what matters, score every option on the same scale, and check whether the ranking survives uncertain assumptions.
walkthroughIntro.bestFor: Several feasible options that need comparison against agreed criteria.
walkthroughIntro.howLong: 26 minutes for 2–6 participants; also available solo.
walkthroughIntro.origin: An independently written workflow using a widely known thinking method. Instructions and fictional examples were created for this app; no third-party endorsement is claimed.

lenses.name: Define criteria and weights
lenses.instruction: Propose measurable criteria and weights that total 100. Define a 1-to-5 scale for each: 1 is least desirable and 5 most desirable. Keep cost direction explicit. Agree the shared criteria and anchors before the next round.

lenses.name: Check comparable options
lenses.instruction: List the feasible options against the agreed constraints. Note missing facts for each option and assumptions that could make a comparison unfair. Confirm the same option labels for everyone.

lenses.name: Score, calculate and challenge
lenses.instruction: Record a row per option: criterion scores from 1 to 5, evidence or assumption for each score, and total = sum(weight × score) / 100. Use the agreed weights. Compare totals, then recalculate under one plausible changed score or weight. Record arithmetic in your answer.

blocks.title: Agree the question
blocks.prompt: Name the decision, constraints and feasible options, including doing nothing where useful. Exclude options that break a non-negotiable constraint before scoring.

walkthrough.whatHappens: The group agrees the question and boundaries before contributing.
walkthrough.whyItMatters: A shared question keeps the later comparisons relevant.

helper.systemPrompt: Coach the participant on this task: Propose measurable criteria and weights that total 100. Define a 1-to-5 scale for each: 1 is least desirable and 5 most desirable. Keep cost direction explicit. Agree the shared criteria and anchors before the next round. Ask one short question about their own reasoning. Do not supply an answer to their real problem. blocks.title: Choose the next step
blocks.prompt: State the selected option and the shared criteria, weights and scores. Show weighted totals and one sensitivity calculation. Explain any choice that differs from the highest score.

criteria.text: Options are scored against the same named criteria, scale and weights totaling 100.

scoring.zero: No common criteria or scoring scale is stated.
scoring.one: A common scale is stated but weights are missing, inconsistent, or do not total 100.
scoring.two: All options use the same named criteria and scale, with weights explicitly totaling 100.

criteria.text: Weighted totals follow the stated formula and identify the preferred feasible option.

scoring.zero: No weighted calculation supports the selected option, or the stated arithmetic contradicts the ranking.
scoring.one: Totals are given but the formula, feasibility check, or preferred option is unclear.
scoring.two: Calculations follow the stated formula, e.g. score times weight divided by 100, and select the highest-ranked feasible option.

criteria.text: A plausible changed assumption is recalculated and its effect on the ranking is discussed.

scoring.one: A changed weight or score is proposed but the ranking is not recalculated.
scoring.two: A plausible weight or score change is recalculated and the resulting ranking change or stability is explained.

walkthrough.whatHappens: Participants propose and vote on a conclusion. Review checks the method-specific criteria; solo sessions can use the same checklist.
walkthrough.whyItMatters: A choice should explain its reasoning and limits.

blocks.title: Assign the follow-through
blocks.prompt: Choose an owner, first action, due date and observable success signal.

walkthrough.whatHappens: The group assigns one person the first action and records when and how to check it.
walkthrough.whyItMatters: An owner and a check make the conclusion actionable.

walkthrough.whatHappens: The engine saves the contributions, conclusion and commitment as reports.
walkthrough.whyItMatters: The record makes assumptions and follow-through available for review.
